candidate_evidence.quote: The objective of this pilot study is to evaluate the efficacy of adding S-Gboxin to standard RT/TMZ treatment protocols in patients with glioblastoma multiforme (GBM) or midline glioma (DMG)

coder_notes: Treatment setting is internally inconsistent: eligibility requires relapse or progression, but the summary describes adding S-Gboxin to standard RT/TMZ (a first-line regimen) and the arm label says 'during (or without) standard treatment'; coded recurrent from eligibility. Temozolomide is not a registered intervention but is named as the standard backbone; listed as soc_backbone; whether every patient receives it is unclear ('or without'). Regimen coded combination on that basis. H3K27M row: DMG H3 K27M-mutant is one eligible histology (title says 'regardless of mutation status'), not a strict entry requirement for all; may be dropped. Target engagement coded yes because the primary outcome is tumour metabolism on PET for a metabolic (OXPHOS) inhibitor; could be read as imaging response. S-Gboxin registered as Biological but is a small molecule; may be a salt/formulation of gboxin.
